text:
Maya R: Customer on Dedicated reported intermittent 429s even though they have a reserved pool (pool-id: rp-8a3f). They see bursts for ~30s and then things recover. Asking for repro steps + quick mitigation they can apply.

Alex K: Can you paste a sample of the failing request (headers + throughput) and the customer-visible error body?

Maya R: Error body: "status:429, code:POOL_EXHAUSTED, message:\"burst capacity exhausted\""
Headers they sent: 
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-prod
X-Redwood-Pool: rp-8a3f
Content-Type: application/json
```
Throughput: sustained 180 qps for 45s with 500ms median latency; spikes up to 650 qps for ~20s. Model: redwood-7b-v2.

Ian (support): Sounds like token-bucket headroom hit. Are they on a config with burst_headroom=0.15? If headroom is low bursts will get throttled even if reserved throughput nominally covers average.

Maya R: Customer config shows reserved_qps=200, burst_headroom=0.05. They thought reserved pool would absorb the spikes.

Alex K: That headroom is tiny. Quick mitigation: increase burst_headroom to 0.25 or enable burst_pool_bypass for short windows. Also check that their client is not sending very large concurrent connections that defeat pipeline batching.

Leah P: Also verify auth routing. If requests are routed to fallback (shared) pool due to token mismatch the reserved pool won't be used. Run this query in Grafana/Prometheus to confirm routing:
```
sum by(pool, status) (rate(redwood_requests_total{pool=~"rp-.*"}[1m]))
```
and check redwood_pool_rejects_total{pool="rp-8a3f"}.

Maya R: Ran the query, saw rejects spike aligned with customer timeline. rejects_total increased by ~260 during the 20s spike. The instance logs contain:
```
[2026-02-04T15:03:12Z] pool=rp-8a3f token=VALID route=dedicated serve_ms=12 status=200
[2026-02-04T15:03:18Z] pool=rp-8a3f token=VALID route=dedicated serve_ms=18 status=429 reason=TOKEN_BUCKET_EMPTY
[2026-02-04T15:03:25Z] pool=rp-8a3f token=VALID route=dedicated serve_ms=15 status=429 reason=TOKEN_BUCKET_EMPTY
```
Looks like token bucket drained mid-spike.

Ian (support): For repro, tell SRE to replay the pattern from a load generator: steady 180 qps + a 20s 650 qps burst. Use this curl loop to simulate (basic):
```
for i in {1..700}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-prod" -H "X-Redwood-Pool: rp-8a3f" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
sleep 0.02
done
```
Monitor redwood_pool_tokens_available and redwood_pool_rejects_total.

Alex K: Long term: recommend bumping reserved_qps to 300 for this customer or add burst_allowance window (config: burst_window_secs=30, burst_headroom=0.25). Also schedule a canary to verify latency SLOs under new config.

Leah P: I'll file a ticket to change pool config temporarily and follow up with metrics. Ticket: RDW-4789 (increase rp-8a3f headroom, enable short burst window).

Maya R: Customer ok with temporary change. Can on-call apply change now? If not, provide them a mitigation: add an exponential backoff that caps client-side concurrency to 300 connections and spread retries over 5s.

sre-bot: NOTE: Applying pool config requires a 2-minute rolling restart of the pool router; expect ~1% p99 jitter during rollout.

Ian (support): I'll coordinate with infra on-call. If we see auth routing issues too, check client is sending X-Redwood-Pool header consistently and not rotating keys across multiple pools.

Maya R: Thanks — adding repro steps and the curl script to the ticket. Will update customer after infra confirms change. :thumbsup:

Alex K: Also include the PromQL snippets and the log lines in the ticket. Good triage.
